debates.t: Scheduling the Rescheduled 751 South / Southern Durham Development Corp. Public Hearing (June 1 vs. June 23 vs. June 24)
debates.s: Commissioners clashed over when to hold the deferred 751 South public hearing requested by K&L Gates, weighing whether to keep the June 1 date after an appeal withdrawal, grant the full 30-day maximum to June 24, or pick June 23 amid budget sessions and personal travel conflicts.
debates.sa: Schedule the hearing on Wednesday, June 23, 2010 at 7:00 PM to stay within the 30-day UDO window and accommodate most schedules.
debates.sb: Hold the hearing either on June 24 (as requested by K&L Gates) or earlier in June (June 1 or the first/second week of June).

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
debates.t: City-County Planning Commission Seat-Shifting & City-County Appearance Commission Tie
debates.s: During Item 10 board appointments, commissioners disputed the fairness of Planning Commission nominations (including Linda Smith's non-reappointment, Darius Little remaining on the ballot, and shifting a member from an at-large seat to an Oak Grove seat), and deadlocked 2-2 on the City-County Appearance Commission appo
debates.sa: Maintain existing ballot slates and proceed with appointments or shift seats as proposed, declining to change votes on the tied Appearance Commission seat.
debates.sb: Object to 'stacking the deck' and shifting applicants across seats without re-advertising, and decline to reconsider Appearance Commission votes.

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
debates.t: Whether to Include Outside Experts at Initial Strategic Planning Session
debates.s: Commissioners disagreed over how to structure a proposed May strategic planning session requested by Commissioner Brenda A. Howerton—specifically whether to invite outside resource people on the first day or review written examples internally first.
debates.sa: Bring in resource people to outline strategic planning possibilities and categories (economic development, human services, community revitalization) for the Boa
debates.sb: Object to bringing outside experts to the first session and instead distribute written strategic plans from comparable jurisdictions to read beforehand.

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
debates.t: Workforce Development Board Appointment Process and Candidate Selection (Ms. Henry vs. Donald Hughes)
debates.s: Commissioners clashed over the Workforce Development Board appointment process after documents were placed at seats shortly before the meeting and department director Kevin Dick contacted candidate Donald Hughes about serving on a subordinate committee while favoring Ms. Henry as Youth Council chair.
debates.sa: Appoint Ms. Henry based on her prior Youth Council service and early application so she could serve as Youth Council chair.
debates.sb: Object to bypassing commissioner board liaisons, dropping late materials at seats, and telling Donald Hughes he must serve on a committee before joining the boa

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
debates.t: Interlocal Agreement with Durham Public Schools for Capital/Lottery Sales Tax Reimbursements (Item 9)
debates.s: Commissioners clashed over an amended interlocal agreement allowing Durham Public Schools to capture sales tax reimbursements through the county on lottery-funded and non-bond capital projects, passing 4-1 amid objections over circumventing state law and unanswered procedural questions.
debates.sa: Approve the amended interlocal agreement to save DPS $180,000–$300,000 and maintain county accountability.
debates.sb: Oppose the agreement as an improper circumvention of state legislative policy and object to voting before written answers on urgency were provided.

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
debates.t: CJRC / Former Jail Renovation Contract and Contingency Cap
debates.s: Commissioners split 3-2 over approving the $2.193M CJRC renovation contract with a reduced 10% contingency cap.
debates.sa: Approve the construction contract while tightening the contingency cap from 15% to 10% ($210,000) to control project cost creep.
debates.sb: Oppose either the capital expenditure altogether amid fiscal pressure (Bowser) or oppose restricting staff's 15% contingency allowance (Page).

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
debates.t: Consular ID Language in Bill of Rights / Human Rights Day Resolution
debates.s: Commissioners divided 4-1 over adopting a Sheriff-negotiated resolution that omitted explicit acceptance of Matrícula Consular and foreign government IDs.
debates.sa: Adopt the revised resolution affirming equal policing regardless of immigration status as a constructive first step without compelling the Sheriff to accept unv
debates.sb: Oppose (or defer) the diluted resolution because immigrant community advocates requested retention of consular ID recognition.

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
debates.t: Public Disclosure vs. Closed Session for Jordan Lake Protest Petition Review
debates.s: Commissioners split 2-2 on hearing an open-session explanation of why the Jordan Lake rezoning protest petition was invalidated and 3-1 on discussing the matter in closed session.
debates.sa: Provide an open-session factual report from the County Attorney explaining why citizen protest petition signatures were ruled invalid.
debates.sb: Restrict legal discussion of the protest petition and Southern Durham Development Inc. v. Durham County to closed session.

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
debates.t: Elementary School F Land Acquisition and Bond Transfer ($1.87M)
debates.s: Commissioners split 3-1 over purchasing 33.2 acres on South Roxboro Road for a future elementary school.
debates.sa: Purchase the discounted 33.2-acre parcel now using transferred bond funds to relieve five overcrowded southern elementary schools.
debates.sb: Oppose purchasing land during a fiscal downturn when construction funding is unavailable and site rock-blasting poses risks.

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
debates.t: Jordan Lake Critical Area Boundary Adjustments (A09-00004 & Z09-00009 / 751 South)
debates.s: Commissioners divided 3-2 over shifting Jordan Lake watershed protection boundaries across ~835 acres in southern Durham County based on an applicant-funded survey accepted by NC DWQ, despite unanimous Planning Commission denial and an invalidated protest petition.
debates.sa: Approve A09-00004 and Z09-00009 using the NC Division of Water Quality-accepted survey rather than outdated 1980s USGS quad maps, expanding economic tax base wh
debates.sb: Reject the boundary shifts until an independent county-funded survey validates the mapping, adhering to the Planning Commission (12-0) and EAB recommendations t

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
debates.t: Use of Community Health Trust Fund Reserves for Bahama VFD Paramedics (Item 5B)
debates.s: Commissioner Bowser dissented 4-1 against appropriating $133,192 from the Community Health Trust Fund to support Bahama Volunteer Fire Department paramedic services.
debates.sa: Approve $133,192 from the Community Health Trust Fund to fund emergency paramedic coverage in northern Durham.
debates.sb: Oppose spending down principal reserves in the Community Health Trust Fund.

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
debates.t: Multi-Year Renewal Authority on Triangle WWTP Chemical Contracts (Item 7G)
debates.s: Commissioners split 4-1 over giving the County Manager authority to renew wastewater treatment plant chemical contracts annually for up to five years without annual Board bidding or approval.
debates.sa: Approve one-year chemical contracts with up to five annual manager renewals for operational stability and volume pricing.
debates.sb: Limit delegation to two or three years rather than five years so the Board annually reviews vendor pricing and minority/women business participation.

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
debates.t: Indefinite Deferral of New Middle School B Rezoning (Northern Durham / Treyburn)
debates.s: Commissioners voted 4-1 to grant DPS's deferral request on New Middle School B so school officials could assemble site-plan data and negotiate with Treyburn-area neighbors, while Commissioner Bowser opposed deferral.
debates.sa: Defer the rezoning without a fixed return date to encourage creative compromise between DPS and neighborhood residents.
debates.sb: Vote against deferment because the donated land parcel sits directly behind existing homes and cannot realistically win neighborhood consent.

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Budget Worksession
debates.t: Board of County Commissioners Travel Budget Allocation and Individual Caps
debates.s: Commissioners disagreed during the budget wrap-up session over whether to cap individual commissioner travel at $3,000 each within a $15,000 pool or allocate $4,000 per member ($20,000) to support national/state conference participation.
debates.sa: Support a higher travel allocation ($4,000 per commissioner or flexible pool) to cover state and national conferences, committee leadership duties, and new-comm
debates.sb: Restrict the Board's travel budget (e.g., $15,000 total / $3,000 per commissioner cap) to set an example of fiscal restraint.

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
debates.t: Jordan Lake 216 MSL Normal Pool Line / Watershed Overlay Map Amendment Process (Public Hearing vs. Administrative Correction)
debates.s: The Board split 3-2 over whether updating the Jordan Lake 216-foot normal pool watershed overlay boundary affecting over 300 parcels required statutory and UDO public hearing map-amendment procedures or could be executed administratively without a public hearing.
debates.sa: Require full statutory and Unified Development Ordinance map-amendment procedures, including public hearings, as recommended by the County Manager, County Attor
debates.sb: Treat the 216 MSL boundary update as an administrative map correction based on the February 4, 2009 Division of Water Quality letter and January 6, 2006 Plannin

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Special Session
debates.t: Jordan Lake Watershed Boundary: Administrative Map Correction vs. Formal Zoning Amendment
debates.s: Commissioners Joe W. Bowser and Ellen W. Reckhow took opposing positions on whether implementing the state-approved Jordan Lake normal-pool boundary survey should be handled as an administrative map correction or as a formal zoning map and comprehensive plan amendment. The transcript explicitly notes Bowser and Reckhow
debates.sa: Treat the revised Jordan Lake watershed delineation as a map correction to existing boundaries based on updated survey data.
debates.sb: Treat the revision as a formal zoning and comprehensive plan amendment requiring Planning Commission review, property-owner notice, public hearing, and Board vo

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
debates.t: County Hiring Freeze Enforcement on Senior Administrative Vacancies vs. Frontline Positions
debates.s: Commissioners Joe W. Bowser and Becky M. Heron differed on how strictly to freeze outgoing Assistant Director positions in Public Health and Social Services versus waiting for spring sales tax data and department harm assessments.
debates.sa: Do not refill outgoing Assistant Director vacancies in Public Health and Social Services until the budget improves, stop freezing frontline roles while filling
debates.sb: Hold off on replacements for 3–4 months until March sales tax revenues and the July 1 budget are clearer, maintaining the Public Health freeze while allowing So

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
debates.t: Mid-Year Reallocation of $75,000 Eno River Open Space Funds and Nonprofit vs. Animal Shelter / Open Space Cuts
debates.s: Following public appeals from Open Space, Farmland Protection, and Urban Ministries homeless shelter advocates regarding mid-year FY 2008–2009 budget cuts, board members debated whether $75,000 freed from a past Eno River open space exchange should go to homeless shelter support or remain in Open Space, as well as the
debates.sa: Direct the $75,000 Eno River open space refund toward homeless shelter support and prioritize human shelter needs over animal shelter funding.
debates.sb: Keep the $75,000 in Open Space/Farmland Protection where it originated and recognize the County's ongoing investments in both Urban Ministries and 24/7 animal s

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
debates.t: Immediate Authorization vs. Deferral of $100,000 Comprehensive Jordan Lake Shoreline Survey
debates.s: Commissioners disagreed sharply over whether to immediately authorize $100,000 for a detailed county-wide Jordan Lake shoreline survey (with 10-to-50-foot intervals) or defer the expenditure to the newly elected Board taking office in December.
debates.sa: Defer action on the $100,000 comprehensive survey until the new Board convenes and considers it in the budget or future meetings.
debates.sb: Immediately approve the County Manager's recommendation and budget amendment for an independent, comprehensive shoreline survey.

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
debates.t: Submission of Jordan Lake Watershed Boundary Revisions to NC DWQ Without Public Hearing or Comprehensive Survey
debates.s: Following closed session near 10:00 PM, the Board split 3-2 on directing the Planning Director to submit a 2005 developer survey and 2006 planning memorandum revising Jordan Lake watershed overlay boundaries to state regulators.
debates.sa: Immediately submit the 2005 Puckett & Associates survey, boundary maps, and January 6, 2006 Frank Duke memorandum to NC DWQ/EMC to cure a procedural defect on a
debates.sb: Oppose late-night action without a public hearing and instead pursue a uniform, comprehensive survey of the Jordan Lake shoreline.

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
debates.t: Durham County Animal Control Ordinance Anti-Tethering Restrictions and Pen Size Mandate
debates.s: Commissioners split 4-1 on adopting Chapter 4 Animal Control Ordinance amendments restricting tethering and expanding unobstructed dog enclosure requirements.
debates.sa: Adopt the amended anti-tethering and minimum pen-size ordinance while pairing implementation with an education campaign and APS/coalition fence assistance.
debates.sb: Oppose the new ordinance as lacking Durham-specific empirical proof and creating undue hardship for elderly and low-income residents.

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
debates.t: Opposition to Proposed National Bio and Agro-Defense Facility (NBAF) in Granville County / Butner
debates.s: The Board split 4-1 on whether to strengthen its Environmental Affairs Board draft EIS comments into formal opposition asking the consortium to withdraw the proposed Butner NBAF site.
debates.sa: Formally oppose locating the NBAF facility in Butner/Granville County and request that the consortium withdraw the proposal.
debates.sb: Submit the Environmental Affairs Board's technical Draft EIS comments by the August 25 deadline without taking a formal vote of opposition at this stage.

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
debates.t: Deferral of Residential Development / Zoning Proposal (Parking, Carrying Costs, and Planning Commission Recommendation)
debates.s: Commissioners split 4-1 over deferring a residential development proposal for two weeks after debating sewer line carrying costs, parking reduction/two-car garage design, and adherence to the Planning and Zoning Commission's recommendation.
debates.sa: Defer the development proposal for two weeks for additional revisions and direction on parking and project design.
debates.sb: Opposed the two-week deferral motion.

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
debates.t: Durham County Memorial Stadium Architectural Design Contract ($646,275)
debates.s: Commissioners split 3-1 over executing a $646,275 architectural design contract with DTW Architects and Planners for renovations to Durham County Memorial Stadium following Shaw University's withdrawal from participation.
debates.sa: Approve the design contract to upgrade Durham County Memorial Stadium and attract broader community and event use.
debates.sb: Oppose spending $646,275 on stadium renovation design.

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
debates.t: $4.5 Million General Fund Balance Advance for Durham County Memorial Stadium Renovations (Item 7H)
debates.s: During consideration of the July 23, 2007 consent agenda, Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek objected to advancing $4.5 million from General Fund balance for the Durham County Memorial Stadium renovation project and asked to be recorded as voting No, prompting the Board to pull Item 7H and approve it 3-1.
debates.sa: Advance $4.5 million from General Fund balance (to be reimbursed via spring 2008 financing) to move forward with Durham County Memorial Stadium renovations.
debates.sb: Oppose advancing $4.5 million in county funds for the Memorial Stadium renovation project.

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
debates.t: Cost and Fiscal Timing of DSS Lease Agreement with Genesis Home
debates.s: Commissioners split 3-1 over approving a $45,000-per-year (plus utilities) DSS lease for 4,400 square feet at Genesis Home, weighing family support needs against taxpayer sensitivity before the November bond referendum.
debates.sa: Approve the DSS lease with Genesis Home to support family reunification and frontline social workers.
debates.sb: Oppose the lease as an expensive expenditure given taxpayer frustration and upcoming bond votes.

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
debates.t: County Ordinance Prohibiting Roadway Solicitation
debates.s: Commissioners split 3-1 on enacting a ban on roadway solicitation in unincorporated Durham County paired with a resource list for deputies, debating pedestrian safety and outreach versus potential punitive enforcement against homeless individuals without a parallel city ordinance.
debates.sa: Enact the county roadway solicitation ban paired with a social-service resource sheet for deputies.
debates.sb: Oppose enacting the county ban at this time without a joint city-county framework and stronger homeless services.

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
debates.t: R-20 Rezoning / Development Application with Technical Ordinance Violation and Neighborhood Mediation Impasse
debates.s: Commissioners deadlocked 2-2 over whether to vote to approve a disputed R-20 development application adjacent to game lands after a nine-month delay, amid planning staff findings of a technical ordinance violation and County Attorney warnings of litigation risk.
debates.sa: Bring the R-20 application to a vote for approval on the floor.
debates.sb: Oppose approving the application as submitted.

debates.mt: Board of County Commissioners' Regular Session
debates.t: Removal and Re-Advertisement of Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority Appointments Under Term-Limit Policy (Item 10)
debates.s: The Board split 3-2 on Commissioner Lewis A. Cheek's motion, seconded by Vice Chair Becky M. Heron, to remove and re-advertise the Raleigh-Durham Airport Authority appointments because incumbent Steve Toler appeared to have served beyond the Board's three-consecutive-term limit policy, while Commissioners Michael D. Pa
debates.sa: Remove the RDU Airport Authority appointment item and re-advertise the positions so the Board can follow its adopted term-limit policy and review all applicants
debates.sb: Opposed removing and re-advertising the RDU Airport Authority appointments instead of proceeding with the scheduled appointments.
